# Test fixtures: one authored Atmos scene, encoded twice

Two short bitstreams of the same synthetic programme, so that CI can run
`oadec decode --format adm` and `--format damf` end to end without any film
material. Everything here was generated from `authored-scene.json`; nothing is
copied from a commercial title.

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 | How |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `authored-scene.json` | 1 372 | `1c12a6255439012927293e83b467edb98085bc02014fd6791f6eff7e0c0316c7` | the scene, written by hand |
| `authored-scene.ec3` | 112 896 | `c4481f2599328b3c21c98b9f8390bca7ec448077937bf41f74f834ce89f9efe8` | Dolby Encoding Engine 5.2.1, job `fixture-joc.xml` (E-AC-3 JOC, 448 kbit/s) |
| `authored-scene.mlp` | 546 456 | `d782d604093578e8c73a190e37ef7a6f7a4b5b7421cfaa274f9bfd406b026061` | Dolby Encoding Engine 5.2.1, job `fixture-thd.xml` (TrueHD Atmos, 12 spatial clusters) |
| `fixture-joc.xml`, `fixture-thd.xml` | | `093e98de811a516936d87a9165a85434636bdebcdffef11cda6d8e6219960388`, `cd81ee244a5500565fd34d95197c50d5a0f4e772df27c41e931b0b0499143343` | the DEE jobs, verbatim but for the work directory's name (their paths name where they ran) |

## DVD-Audio (FBB) streams

Four short MLP streams in the DVD-Audio (FBB) syntax, written by FFmpeg's MLP
encoder (`ffmpeg version 2026-10-12-git-615b07170e`, `-c:a mlp -strict -2`)
from sine tones, one frequency per channel, placed by an explicit `join` map so
that each tone names the channel it was written to. `tests/cli_fbb.rs` decodes
them and holds each tone to its label and the decoded bytes to FFmpeg's own
decode of the same stream (24-bit, interchange order, FNV-1a 64).

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 | Channels and tones | FFmpeg's decode, FNV-1a 64 |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `mlp-stereo-44k.mlp` | 10 472 | `d843bdf1bef8d4ded7501eb02a4ae50d6f87733c4febd06f9fc7b555c66c5092` | L 440 Hz R 660 Hz | `0x800e01e817c7134d` |
| `mlp-51-96k.mlp` | 21 916 | `cfb5af1ddcc23afe2997e75d9f13e69f693df75984197e9f90a1fae14a918ade` | L 300 Hz R 500 Hz C 700 Hz LFE 60 Hz Lb 900 Hz Rb 1100 Hz | `0x158f143f61501695` |
| `mlp-quad-48k.mlp` | 9 314 | `d44b476ac7da848ae700af4070471946f62d2558809f3a2b1623d570e4ccb196` | L 300 Hz R 500 Hz Lb 900 Hz Rb 1100 Hz | `0x139ee67d2f836675` |
| `mlp-41-48k.mlp` | 11 304 | `12fe9226032f17149a6a8826d0466ce3ddf8e9fc9b94253b7046276451281325` | L 300 Hz R 500 Hz C 700 Hz LFE 60 Hz Cb 1300 Hz | `0xabbc713773af9409` |

FFmpeg's encoder writes every channel into one substream, whatever the
layout: these streams carry one presentation, assignments 1, 12, 3 and 11.

## TrueHD at the 44.1 kHz family and 192 kHz

No title in the library carries TrueHD at 44.1, 88.2 or 176.4 kHz, or at 192
kHz. Four short streams at those rates were written by FFmpeg's TrueHD encoder
(`ffmpeg version 2026-10-12-git-615b07170e`, `-c:a truehd -strict -2`) from
sine tones, 0.1 s, one frequency per channel, generated by `aevalsrc` with one
expression per channel in the layout's own order and written to 24-bit PCM
first. `tests/cli_rates.rs` holds each decode to FFmpeg's (24-bit, interchange
order, FNV-1a 64), which is the encoder's input sample for sample; each tone to
its label; and the rate to what `info --json` and the WAVE header say.

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 | Rate | Channels and tones | FFmpeg's decode, FNV-1a 64 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| `truehd-20-44k.thd` | 13 454 | `2917dfe7d26ce3b95f39c0dacc7d36434bb851fb83fd37b7d7494548ed55a9fe` | 44 100 | L 440 Hz R 660 Hz | `0xc4a646d6b4645e25` |
| `truehd-51-88k.thd` | 59 202 | `687e31f3dc74424c0ba9b9cc668841c43681e3ff92f2d0f4eced1dfe64282ac7` | 88 200 | L 300 Hz R 500 Hz C 700 Hz LFE 60 Hz Ls 900 Hz Rs 1100 Hz | `0x7cbbca61b9a3e5fd` |
| `truehd-20-176k.thd` | 36 932 | `548a285b86795c673f3b2180f42e813c30400ac92aea45b68ca99d503e26a97d` | 176 400 | L 440 Hz R 660 Hz | `0x26e6fa9cc45fdf35` |
| `truehd-20-192k.thd` | 39 470 | `b01ed3a53268d69d4312e2fdf4dedbb22d7037875fa69fa54e7ad6eee361f41b` | 192 000 | L 440 Hz R 660 Hz | `0xf6ef145eb7c06a4d` |

## The scene

Two seconds at 48 kHz, a silent LFE bed and six objects, each a sine at
−30 dBFS that identifies it by frequency, or impulses:

| Object | Signal | Metadata |
|---|---|---|
| front-left static | 440 Hz | (−1, 1, 0) |
| front-right static | 660 Hz | (1, 1, 0) |
| top centre static | 880 Hz | (0, 0, 1) |
| left to right in one second | 1320 Hz | five positions from (−1, 0, 0) to (1, 0, 0) at 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 1.979 s |
| rear centre at minus six | 1760 Hz | (0, −1, 0), gain −6 dB |
| impulses front centre | impulses at 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 s, −20 dBFS | (0, 1, 0) |

The encoder re-times and clusters the metadata (the TrueHD encode carries
11 objects, the JOC encode 15, both with 1536-sample ramps), so the decoded
outputs are compared with each other and against what the scene makes certain
(track identity by frequency, event order, the ramps the profile replaces), not
sample by sample with the authoring master. DEE applies the authored gain into
the object audio and writes 0 dB, so the −6 dB object arrives 6 dB quieter with
no gain field; that is the encoder's behaviour, established in the remediation
report of 2026-09-10.

## Regenerating

```
oadec atmos-author authored-scene.json -o authored-scene
dee\dee.exe --xml fixture-joc.xml     # writes authored-scene.ec3
dee\dee.exe --xml fixture-thd.xml     # writes authored-scene.mlp
```

The jobs expect the DAMF set and the outputs under
`oadec-work\audit\adm\remed\fixture`; adjust the four `<path>` elements
for another machine. A regenerated encode is not guaranteed byte-identical to
the committed one; the tests assert structure and identity, not the encoder's
bytes.
